UT is "Ultrasonic Testing." And IMO it's one of the most fun/challenging NDT methods. You use a transducer which has a "crystal" (used to be crystals, now it's usually some acrylic blend) to vibrate at an extremely rapid rate and that produces and ultrasonic sound wave. The sound wave "bounces" around the piece you are inspecting and when it hits a discontinuity it shows up on your display. There are, basically, three types of display. A, B, and C scan. A scan display B scan display C scan display This method is very accurate but hard to master. The two main types of "waves" used are shear wave and longitudinal (straight beam). Straight beam, as the name suggest, causes particles in the material to propagate in a straight line, like those metal clackers people have on their office desk. Shear wave is a basically a wave that causes particles in the material to move in a right angle. Read more here: https://www.nde-ed.org/EducationResources/CommunityCollege/Ultrasonics/Physics/wavepropagation.htm
